title: The Synergy Of Humans And AI Is Reshaping The Workforce For The Future
text:
Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative force, altering the way businesses operate and compete. Contrary to the dystopian narrative that AI will lead to widespread job displacement, a more nuanced and likely scenario is unfolding. It is not AI alone that will replace people, but rather people equipped with AI tools who will replace those who are not. This paradigm shift underscores the importance of integrating AI into the workforce, highlighting how the symbiosis between humans and AI can redefine productivity, efficiency, and creativity. This blog explores how this integration will reshape the workforce and define the future of work, examining both the positive and negative implications of this transition.
Why AI Augments Rather Than Replaces Human Capabilities
AI excels at processing vast amounts of data, identifying patterns, and performing repetitive tasks with unparalleled speed and accuracy. However, AI lacks the nuanced understanding, emotional intelligence, and creative problem-solving abilities inherent to humans. The future of work lies not in choosing between human or AI capabilities but in leveraging the strengths of both. When humans harness AI as a tool, they enhance their own skill sets, leading to increased productivity, innovation, and decision-making capabilities.
Positive Changes in the Workforce
To begin with, organizations will reap enhanced productivity and efficiency. AI tools can automate routine tasks, freeing up humans to focus on complex problem-solving, strategic planning, and creative endeavors. This division of labor maximizes efficiency and productivity, allowing businesses to achieve more with the same resources.
In addition, enterprises expect increased innovation. By analyzing data and trends, AI can identify opportunities for innovation that might not be immediately apparent to humans. When people use AI to guide their explorations, they can push the boundaries of creativity, leading to breakthroughs in products, services, and processes.
Furthermore, companies look to AI for improved decision making. AI's ability to process and analyze data at scale enhances human decision-making. People using AI can access insights and predictions based on comprehensive data analysis, leading to more informed and strategic choices.
In addition, this creates the opportunity for personalized learning and development. AI can tailor learning experiences to individual workers, identifying skills gaps and recommending personalized training. This fosters a culture of continuous learning and adaptability, crucial for staying relevant in a rapidly changing job market.
Finally, there is the creation of new job categories. As AI takes over routine tasks, new roles will emerge that focus on managing, interpreting, and leveraging AI technologies. This evolution will lead to the creation of jobs that we can scarcely imagine today, driving forward economic growth and innovation.
Negative Changes and Challenges
However, integrating AI into business poses drawbacks as well. First, there is the inevitable issue of skill disparities and job displacement. The divide between those who can effectively use AI and those who cannot, will lead to job displacement and widening skill gaps. Workers unable to adapt to AI-driven environments may find themselves at a disadvantage, highlighting the need for widespread AI literacy and retraining programs.
Second, this will lead to further AI usage concerns on ethics and privacy. Integrating AI into the workplace raises ethical questions around surveillance, data privacy, and the potential for algorithmic bias. Businesses must navigate these issues carefully to maintain trust and ensure fair treatment of employees.
Third, the workforce will see increased pressure on the workers. The efficiency and productivity gains from AI could lead to heightened expectations for human workers, potentially increasing stress and workloads. Balancing AI's capabilities with human well-being will be a critical challenge for organizations.
Fourth, the issues on the digital divide, particularly economic inequality, will increase. The benefits of AI may disproportionately favor those with the skills and resources to leverage it, exacerbating economic inequality. Addressing this disparity requires concerted efforts from governments, educational institutions, and businesses to ensure broad access to AI training and opportunities.
Strategies for a Successful Integration of AI into the Workforce
To navigate the transition towards an AI-augmented workforce successfully, several strategies must be implemented:
· Invest in AI Literacy and Skills Training: Businesses and educational institutions must prioritize AI literacy, offering training programs to equip workers with the skills needed to collaborate with AI technologies effectively.
· Develop Ethical AI Guidelines: Organizations should establish clear ethical guidelines for AI use that prioritize transparency, fairness, and privacy, ensuring that AI tools are used responsibly.
· Foster a Culture of Continuous Learning: Encouraging a mindset of continuous learning and adaptability among employees will be key to navigating the evolving work landscape. Supporting workers through transitions and encouraging experimentation with AI tools can cultivate a resilient and innovative workforce.
· Implement Supportive Policies and Infrastructure: Governments and businesses should collaborate to create policies and infrastructures that support workers displaced or affected by AI, including retraining programs, social safety nets, and incentives for businesses to invest in human capital.
The integration of AI into the workforce presents both significant opportunities and challenges. The future will not be about AI replacing humans but about the synergistic potential of humans and AI working together. Those who embrace and learn to leverage AI will set themselves apart, driving forward innovation, efficiency, and growth. As we stand on the brink of this transformative era, the emphasis must be on preparing the workforce for the future, ensuring that AI serves as a tool for empowerment rather than a source of displacement. By adopting strategic, ethical, and inclusive approaches to AI integration, we can pave the way for a future where the collaboration between humans and AI leads to unprecedented levels of achievement and prosperity.

title: How AI Can Compensate For Age-Related Cognitive Decline
text:
The global population aged 60 and older is projected to nearly double, from 12% to 22%, between 2015 and 2050, according to the World Health Organization. This demographic shift brings with it concerns about cognitive decline, including memory loss and reduced problem-solving abilities, as well as physical decline such as reduced mobility and dexterity.
Cognitive aging is a natural process that affects everyone, albeit to varying degrees. It typically involves declines in processing speed, attention, and memory. These changes can begin as early as our 30s, with more pronounced effects in our 60s and beyond as shown by a 2022 study published in Nature Aging. However, it's crucial to note that cognitive aging is not synonymous with dementia or Alzheimer's disease—it's a normal part of aging that can be managed and, in some cases, partially mitigated.
Whilst there is abundant worry about artificial intelligence, including the fact that it is triggering a wave of destillier, upskilling and reskilling at work. It also has the potential to address both cognitive and physical aspects of aging through various innovative solutions. The key question is how we can leverage AI to age gracefully and maintain our cognitive abilities and effectiveness as we are traveling the journey of life and living well into the second half of it. AI may serve as a companion tool to explore and discover unknown strengths that had been dormant because we didn’t have the opportunity to curate and share them. This time has come.
AI As A Cognitive Assistant
Artificial Intelligence offers promising avenues to support cognitive function in aging individuals. Here are some key areas where AI is making a difference:
Memory Enhancement: AI-powered digital assistants can serve as external memory banks, providing reminders for appointments, medication schedules, and important dates. Older adults can use digital health interventions, including AI-assisted reminders such as Google Assistant or Amazon Alexa, to help them adhere to medication schedules.
Decision Support: Complex decision-making can become more challenging with age. AI systems like IBM Watson and Google Cloud's AI can analyze vast amounts of data and provide summarized insights, helping older leaders make informed decisions more efficiently.
Speech and Language Processing: AI tools like Otter.ai and Fireflies.ai can transcribe and summarize conversations in real-time, helping individuals keep track of important points in meetings or discussions.
Cognitive Training: AI-driven brain-training apps such as Lumosity and Elevate provide personalized exercises targeting specific cognitive domains, potentially slowing cognitive decline. Computerized cognitive training, which often incorporates AI algorithms, also shows promise in improving brain function in healthy older adults.
AI in Health: Early Detection And Management Of Age-Related Diseases
Beyond cognitive support, AI is helping to detect and manage age-related neurodegenerative diseases early. For Parkinson's disease, AI algorithms analyzing voice recordings have shown promise in detecting early signs of the condition. They can identify subtle voice changes indicative of early-stage Parkinson's with an accuracy of over 87%, according to research.
In the realm of Alzheimer's disease, AI is revolutionizing early diagnosis by analyzing images. Since 2023, researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital have been using AI models capable of predicting Alzheimer's disease from a single brain MRI scan with 98% accuracy. These advancements in early detection could significantly improve treatment outcomes and quality of life for millions of aging individuals.
The 2024 US Presidential elections have brought the question of age-related decline to the forefront. This serves as a reminder that time is passing for all of us, and that AI could help to optimize what we make of the remainder.
Ethical Considerations and Limitations
As we explore the potential of AI to support aging individuals, especially those in positions of power, several ethical considerations arise:
Transparency: There's a need for openness about the use of AI assistive technologies, particularly in roles that impact public policy and national security.
Agency and Autonomy: It's crucial to ensure that AI remains a supportive tool rather than a replacement for human judgment and decision-making.
Privacy: The use of AI to monitor cognitive function, including the expansion of neuroscience assets such as brain chips as the one developed by Neuralink raises important privacy concerns that must be carefully addressed.
Practical Takeaways for Professionals
For professionals looking to leverage AI to support cognitive function as they age, consider the following strategies:
Embrace Digital Assistants: Start integrating AI-powered assistants such as Siri or Alexa into your daily routine for scheduling, reminders, and information management.
Use AI to Process Information: Leverage AI tools like ChatGTP or Gemini to summarize lengthy reports or articles, helping you stay informed without cognitive overload. Zoom and Teams offer automated meeting notes.
Engage in AI-Driven Cognitive Training: Incorporate personalized brain-training apps like Headspace into your routine to nurture your overall mindfulness and platforms such as Lumosity to curate specific cognitive skills.
Consider AI Writing Assistants: Tools like GPT-based writing aids can help maintain writing quality and efficiency, particularly useful for those experiencing changes in language processing.
Stay Informed and Adaptable: Keep abreast of new AI technologies overall, especially those designed to support cognitive function and explore with their incorporation into your own workflow. Resources such as AI-focused newsletters or Blogs like Oneusefulthing, as well as industry conferences can be valuable for staying updated.
Be creative !
Use AI to explore uncharted territory within yourself. AI may help you to identify strengths that you always had but never got a chance to reveal. Could generative artificial technologies serve to manifest your dormant creativity?
Ultimately what matters most is for each of us to remain acutely aware that AI is a means to an end, not an end in itself. It is up to us to decide how and why it can serve us – as a person, and as a professional – to be and become our own best selves.
AI cannot halt the aging process, but it offers useful tools to compensate for age-related cognitive changes and detect potential health issues early. But further and beyond – it can serve us to unleash our latent potential to create.
By thoughtfully integrating new technologies into our personal and professional lives, we can potentially extend our productive years and remain not only effective but unique in demanding roles well into later life. As we move forward, it is up to us to balance the benefits of these technologies with ethical considerations, ensuring that AI is a tool for empowerment rather than a crutch to depend on.
It is a slippery slope from using, to over-using to trusting to relying on AI. We choose at which stage of this process we stop.

title: 4 Ways AI Is Driving Mainstream DeFi Adoption
text:
AI and blockchain might appear to be polar opposites. Blockchain technology is deterministic, transparent, and open to everyone, with every transaction recorded immutably on a public ledger. It also has a steep learning curve, requiring users to understand complex protocols.
On the other hand, AI often functions as a "black box," making decisions based on model parameters and learning data sets, providing probabilistic rather than strictly predictable answers. What unites them, however, is that both technologies have become buzzwords in recent years - venture capital funds are running after them, and companies are working hard at implementing them.
While there are not many cases in which the synergy of both is apparent, it holds significant potential for mainstream adoption, especially in decentralized finance. Here is why:
Enhancing DeFi User Adoption
One of the major hurdles for DeFi adoption is its complexity. AI can play a crucial role in simplifying user interactions with DeFi platforms through AI-driven chatbots and virtual assistants that can guide users through complex DeFi protocols, making them more approachable and user-friendly. Maxim Savelyev, CEO at Web3 consulting firm Empathy Consulting, notes “Mainstream users can see only the tip of the iceberg of what DeFi can offer, such as the Coinbase Wallet, while the most powerful tools remain locked within the enthusiast community due to their complexity”.
By analyzing a user's portfolio and behavior, token trends, and whales transactions, AI can offer tailored advice, helping users make informed decisions without needing deep technical knowledge. One example is decentralized hedge fund Numerai that uses AI and machine learning to crowdsource predictions from data scientists, which are then used to trade in the stock market. This approach shows AI's potential to drive investment strategies in a decentralized manner. Additionally, AI-powered platforms like AlphaPoint leverage AI to analyze on-chain data and predict future DeFi asset prices, aiding users in making informed investment decisions.
Fraud Prevention And Audit
With 76 hacks in 2023 resulting in a collective loss of approximately $1.1 billion, according to Chainalysis, security is a paramount concern in DeFi. AI's ability to detect anomalies and suspicious activities in real-time reduces fraud and maintains trust in decentralized platforms. As Lars Nyman of cloud provider CUDO Compute highlights, "AI can increase security through anomaly detection and improve smart contract functionality via predictive analytics." AI can also assist in creating smart contracts, an activity previously reserved for technical practitioners. By verifying smart contracts and identifying potential vulnerabilities, AI ensures higher security standards and boosts trust in blockchain systems.
That way, decentralized exchange Uniswap
Making Blockchain Data Accessible
Blockchain's transparency is one of its greatest strengths, but the sheer volume of data can make it difficult to derive meaningful insights. AI can bridge this gap by processing and summarizing large datasets, making blockchain data more accessible and smart contract execution more effective. Adnan Masood from solutions provider UST underscores the importance of hybrid approaches where AI processes data off-chain while maintaining on-chain integrity. By transforming raw blockchain data into understandable insights, AI can democratize access to information, allowing users to make better decisions.
An example of this is Chainalysis, which uses AI to monitor and analyze blockchain transactions for suspicious activities, thereby enhancing security and making the data more accessible for analysis. Another blockchain protocol, Fetch.ai, integrates AI to optimize transaction timing and processing with the goal to reduce congestion.
Improving Tools For Blockchain Developers
AI can also enhance the quality of life for blockchain developers by providing low-code and copilot-like solutions. These tools can simplify the development process, reduce the need for extensive coding knowledge, and accelerate project timelines. One example is multichain protocol Guru Network, which provides a low-code solution that integrates traditional business process automation engines with AI snippets to streamline the creation of Web3 and AI applications. Developers can use pre-built components and templates, while GPT agents provide real-time, context-aware consultation from documentation and code repositories.
AI can assist in generating smart contracts, debugging code, and predicting potential issues before they arise. This not only speeds up development but also reduces the margin for error, allowing developers to focus on more strategic and innovative aspects of their projects. AI can also help with the creation of smart contracts, making the development process more accessible to non-technical practitioners.
For example, open-source framework OpenZeppelin employs AI to audit smart contracts, identifying bugs and vulnerabilities before deployment. This proactive approach ensures that smart contracts are secure and function as intended, reducing the likelihood of errors and exploits. Similarly, Ocean Protocol uses AI to develop deterministic models that align with blockchain’s deterministic nature, enhancing the overall development process.
AI is transforming the DeFi landscape, bridging the gap between complex financial technologies and everyday users. By enhancing infrastructure, improving user experience, providing robust security measures, and supporting developers, it is making DeFi more accessible and efficient.
As these technologies continue to evolve, we can expect AI to play a more impactful role in the mainstream adoption of DeFi. By leveraging AI's analytical prowess and ability to handle large data sets, DeFi platforms can offer more secure, efficient, and user-friendly financial services, ultimately democratizing finance and empowering users worldwide.

title: Council Post: Skills And Specialties Every Budding Tech Professional Should Master
text:
With technology playing an ever-growing part in how businesses manage internal operations, serve customers, market their products and more, choosing a career in technology is a wise investment in your future, as you’ll likely be eligible to step into a variety of industries and roles—if you focus on the right skills and specialties. In addition to the “hot” tech trends and topics that dominate the headlines, savvy budding tech professionals would be wise to get a thorough grounding in multiple skills and specialties.
Technology changes constantly and it’s important to keep up, but there are also some traits and abilities that will always help you get ahead in a competitive job market. Here, members of Forbes Technology Council discuss some skills and specialties all tech professionals should focus on acquiring and why organizations will value—or always have valued—them so highly.
1. Soft Skills
Focus on soft skills. Soft skills are as important as technical skills for every professional. For example, effective communication is crucial. If you don’t know how to communicate well with your co-workers or your team, it will be difficult to achieve shared goals and succeed in collaborative projects. - Jose Giammattei, Applaudo
2. Artificial Intelligence
The future of the technology sector lies in artificial intelligence, which will be integrated into all aspects of product development, operations and client acquisition. Every tech professional should invest in understanding the essence of AI, how it works, how to use it and the associated risks. - Artin Bogdanov, Walmart
Forbes Technology Council is an invitation-only community for world-class CIOs, CTOs and technology executives. Do I qualify?
3. Adaptability; Continuous Learning
Topics I recommend every tech professional explore are adaptability and continuous learning. The rapid evolution of technology, especially AI, means that the shape of jobs and required skills will constantly change. Developing a mindset geared toward adaptability and a high rate of learning will ensure you can keep up with new tools, methodologies and industry shifts. - Shivani Modi, Konko AI
4. Cybersecurity
I recommend every tech professional learn cybersecurity. With the increasing frequency and sophistication of cyberthreats, understanding cybersecurity is crucial. It ensures you can protect data, maintain privacy and secure systems against attacks. This knowledge is vital across all tech roles and industries, making it a highly relevant and valuable skill for the future. - Ben Gebremeskel, TeckPath
5. Domain-Specific Fundamentals
As a tech professional, mastering essential skills is crucial. Some of the most basic and important technology skills are domain-specific fundamentals. These may include cloud computing, data analysis, and artificial intelligence and machine learning, as well as fundamentals related to product and application development, such as effective product management, cybersecurity and management soft skills. - Chirag Shah, Model N, Inc.
6. Creative Thinking
Creative thinking skills will become increasingly important for tech professionals as our reliance on AI-powered tools grows. The evolution of technological capabilities requires the engagement of uniquely human capabilities that help us solve complex problems and develop innovative responses to new challenges. - Merav Yuravlivker, Data Society
7. A Customer-Centric UX
I would recommend focusing on the user experience and approaching it from a customer-centric point of view. B2B and B2C experience expectations are converging. B2B buyer journeys are beginning to look quite similar to those of B2C consumers—B2B buyers expect you to know what they want, provide them with an exceptional experience and deliver more than just supplier value. - Andrew Kucheriavy, Intechnic
8. AI As A ‘Sidekick’
Understanding how AI works is crucial for every tech professional. Leveraging AI as a “sidekick” can help you stay up to speed on industry trends and continue learning. It enhances problem-solving skills and opens up innovative possibilities, keeping your skill set relevant. - Rachel Lyubovitzky, Setuply, Inc.
9. Curiosity
Curious people read a lot, have multiple interests and tend to keep an open, growth-oriented mind. We’re at a point in time where the rate of change is so fast that many of the skills and knowledge one has are becoming outdated by the hour. So cultivating flexibility, adaptability and a “constant improvement” mindset is paramount. And these traits stem from curiosity. - Boyan Ivanov, StorPool Storage
10. Agility
The most important skill in tech is agility—being open to new ideas and trends, constantly learning, and embracing AI. Staying relevant requires data science and analytics expertise to extract insights from the massive amounts of data we’re generating across industries. A tech professional with a blend of cutting-edge skills and a growth mindset will be well-positioned for the future. - Shaveer Mirpuri, Insite AI
11. Public Speaking
Perhaps the greatest differentiator a tech professional can have is being an effective public speaker. The ability to present insights to an audience in a compelling and memorable way makes a tech professional stand apart from their peers. Perhaps more than any other single skill, it allows the professional’s knowledge to drive people to take action and effect change. - Zach Fuller, Silent Sector
12. Automation
Tech pros can enhance their relevancy by embracing automation. This is a cultural shift; forward-looking IT pros must operate differently than they have before. The goal is to automate decades-old, well-understood tasks that consume a huge portion of operational overhead. IT pros must think of automation first, not look at it as an exotic technology for limited edge cases. - Song Pang, NetBrain Technologies
13. Communicating With Varying Audiences
Learn how to present to and communicate with various groups, not just members of technical teams. You must be able to present your ideas so your audience can understand what you are trying to say. The best engineers are the ones who can communicate with clients, business leaders and technical teams (at all levels). - Wesley Crook, FP Complete
14. Prompt Writing For GenAI
Generative AI has revolutionized research, and being able to craft a nuanced and thoughtful prompt will become an increasingly important skill as GenAI tools continue to progress. The better the prompt, the better the output. Including contextualizing details, relevant background information and careful questions improves research efficiency, uncovers deeper insights and drives innovation. - Todd Fisher, CallTrackingMetrics
15. Principles Of Core Business Functions
Tech leaders often focus on innovation, but it’s crucial that innovation aligns with business goals. Understanding the core principles of marketing, finance and operations equips them to explain technology outcomes in business terms and view problems from different perspectives, ensuring true business value realization. - Amit Singh, Deloitte Consulting LLP
16. Data Analytics
I’d recommend every tech professional learn about data science and analytics. With the exponential growth of data, proficiency in data analysis and interpretation is invaluable for driving informed decision-making and uncovering insights to drive innovation. This skill set is highly sought after across industries and is essential for staying relevant in today’s data-driven world. - Mohit Gupta, Damco Solutions
17. Critical Thinking
The technology workers of tomorrow must blend futuristic visioning with skepticism to balance AI’s great potential with its hype and the impact of potential bad actors. Therefore, critical thinking is the most important skill in an AI-powered world. It involves not just understanding and using technology, but also questioning its implications, assessing its impacts and ensuring its ethical application. - Joseph Ours, Centric Consulting
18. Cloud Computing
I recommend every tech professional learn about cloud computing. As more organizations migrate to cloud-based solutions, understanding cloud architecture, services and best practices is crucial. This knowledge enables tech professionals to design scalable, efficient and cost-effective systems, ensuring they remain competitive and versatile in the evolving tech landscape. - Vamsi Krishna Dhakshinadhi, GrabAgile Inc.
19. Change Management
Looking back on the last 10 to 15 years, it’s remarkable how much the change we’ve seen—economic, social and technological—is directly impacting organizations, their employees and their customers. Understanding and leading through the disruptive nature of change and being able to identify opportunities for transformation are critical to the growth of any professional, especially those who want to lead. - Ed Jennings, Quickbase
20. Quantum Computing And Quantum AI
I believe it’s important for tech professionals to learn about quantum computing and quantum AI. These technologies will revolutionize many industries and provide a significant advantage in the tech world by performing complex tasks faster and opening up new possibilities in data analysis, machine learning and optimization. - Sarah Choudhary, Ice innovations

title: Apple Forced Into Risky AI Gamble With iPhone 16 Pro
text:
Updated July 19 with details on reduced orders in the iPhone 16 supply chain.
With demand for Apple’s iPhone slowing down, how will Tim Cook and his team lure consumers to its ecosystem? Data from analysts CIRP show that demand for the iPhone —specifically the current iPhone 15 model—is lower than that of the iPhone 14 in this quarter. This echoes the pattern of lower demand seen in Q1 2024.
Update: Friday July 19: While there is talk of an artificial intelligence boom when Apple launches its generative AI-capable iPhones, that talk is not yet reflected in the supply chain. Two major component manufacturers in the supply chain are not expecting growth due to increased orders.
Analyst Ming-Chi Kuo reports on earnings calls from TSMC and Largan, and their forecasts for the coming year are similar to last year.
"My understanding is that some suppliers have seen an increase in iPhone 16 orders for 2H24, but from the EMS/assembly perspective, the iPhone 16 orders for 2H24 have not seen much change (about 87 million units), still slightly lower than the 2H23 iPhone 15 orders (about 91 million units)."
With Apple the biggest player in this market, any increased order to cover the upcoming iPhone 16 family would positively impact their projections. As it stands, it’s the same story as 2023; solid sales but nowhere close to unlocking an untapped market thanks to AI.
The report also highlights one way Apple is hoping to turn around sales. But it’s a gamble that asks for patience from the fickle smartphone market.
Apple will be looking towards one key factor in the iPhone 15 family, which is already accelerating Android sales. Generative AI has transformed the view of what a smartphone can offer consumers, from editing photos and videos, through summarising and analysis of text and images, to assisting creativity.
Following the announcement of Apple’s AI plans at June’s Worldwide Developer Conference, shares in the company rose seven percent, primarily on the promise of increased iPhone sales. Because of the high demands generative AI places on hardware and Apple’s push to process as much user data on the user’s device as possible, Apple Intelligence will only run on one existing iPhone model—the iPhone 15 Pro Max.
Consumers without the most expensive iPhone on the market will need to buy the latest iPhone hardware to access the A18 Pro chip specifically designed to support generative AI routines.
Yet the AI that the iPhone is clearly lacking right now will not be available until the first quarter of 2025. Tim Cook and his team will be asking the Apple faithful to buy the smartphone on the promise of receiving the AI at some point in the future.
Meanwhile, all of those benefits are available on Android and have been since Google introduced the idea of an AI-first smartphone in October 2024 during the Pixel 8 launch. With Google’s Pixel 9 family due to be announced in August, Apple’s iPhone will be two generations behind Android’s AI efforts before it has even left the Cupertino stage.
Will consumers be happy to wait for Apple to catch up to the competition, or will they decide that the AI revolution cannot wait? If it’s the former, then Apple’s decision to "go long” should help revitalise sales of the iPhone. But if it’s the latter, the Android ecosystem may have just found Tim Cook’s Achilles heel.
Now read more about Apple’s iPhone 16 and iPhone 16 Pro launch plans...

title: Britain’s AI Startups Look To Record Year As Regulation Looms
text:
Britain’s artificial intelligence startups accounted for 22 percent of venture capital investment in the first half of this year, according to figures published by Dealroom and HSBC Innovation Banking. In money terms that translates into a total of $2.1 billion raised by startups working in the sector against an investment of $9.4 billion across the ecosystem as a whole. According to the report, the momentum is set to continue. The expectation is that investment into AI will have a record breaking year.
The figures illustrate the growing importance of AI within the U.K. innovation economy. And it’s probably not accidental. Britain’s Conservative government - now in opposition - prioritized the development and commercialization of AI technologies. Under an Action Plan published in 2021 funding was set aside to encourage research, industry partnerships and commercialization. In addition, a favorable visa regime was put in place to suck in talent from overseas. The aim was to position the U.K. - admittedly behind the U.S. and China - as a globally important player. That priority is reflected in the apparent enthusiasm of investors.
But what does that mean for startups in the sector? Well, the first thing that has to be said is that overall VC investment is on the up. Following a lackluster 2023 there were tentative signs of recovery in the first quarter of the year and the momentum continued in the May-June period.
Bouncing Off The Bottom
“In the first quarter, we felt we had bounced off the bottom,” says Simon Bumfrey, Head of Technology and Life Sciences at HSBC Innovation Banking, speaking on a Zoom call. “In the second quarter, the bounce continued and there does seem to be forward momentum.”
The $9.4 billion raised by startups in the first half of 2024 was up from $8.1 billion a year earlier. Some comparisons are even more flattering. In the second quarter alone, investment amounted to $4.6 billion, up 36 percent year-on-year and 47 in comparison with the previous quarter.
But Bumfrey has some words of caution. Underneath the headline figures, there are some gaps in the investment picture. “I feel comfortable with the Seed and Series A rounds,” he says. And we are also seeing the return of mega-rounds. But the middle rounds - the Series B and Cs - are not quite so buoyant.”
And as he points out, there is also a possibility that the so-called mega-rounds - which accounted for 45% of VC investment in the second quarter - are distorting headline figures.
Applied AI
But what of AI? With U.S.-owned tech giants such as Google, Microsoft, IBM and OpenAI making much of the running, where can U.K. businesses find a market niche? As the report points out, much of the investment is going into technology designed for clearly identifiable sectors. These include therapeutics, energy, law and finance. Indeed, the biggest mega-round saw automotive driving company Wayve securing $.1.1 billion. “What we are seeing is investment going to AI that is applied in sectors such as sustainability, cleantech, robotics, enterprise software and life sciences,” says Bumfrey. In other words, AI is not a sector in itself but a tool.
There does seem to be considerable investor interest in the commercialisation of University research. Spinouts and startups linked to the universities of Cambridge and Oxford raised the most venture capital outside London in the first half, suggesting a high level of interest not just in AI but in other science-led sectors such as life sciences and quantum.
Coming Regulation
As luck would have it, the Dealroom/HSBC report coincided with the launch of the newly-minted Labour government’s legislative program, which included a statement of intent on the regulation of AI. As set out in the King’s Speech, the government promised to “establish appropriate legislation to place requirements on those working to develop the most powerful artificial intelligence models.”
This certainly wasn’t unexpected. The European Union already has its AI Act and the U.S. is developing legislation. A legal and regulatory framework for the U.K. is therefore, inevitable. However, the unfolding shape of the regulatory regime will be of huge interest to everyone working in a rapidly evolving field.
And it’s a fine balancing act. In a statement responding to the government's statement of intent, VC OpenOcean urged the continuation of a light-touch approach to startups but acknowledged the need for regulation - and the possible benefits. “With international AI regulations such as the EU’s AI Act and California’s SB 1047 already taking shape, the UK Government may look to align with these global standards. In doing so, it can promote interoperable reporting systems and offer a clear roadmap for AI companies operating within the UK,” said General Partner, Ekaterina Almasque,
That’s still a work in progress. In the meantime, AI is continuing to prove popular with VCs althought it's worth remembering that the current round of investment could prove to be something of a bubble. In the meantime, it shouldn’t be forgotten that Fintech - for so long the poster child for Britain’s innovation economy - is still a magnet for capital. Indeed, it was the biggest “aggregate sector” with major players such as Monzo, Abound and Flagstone among the mega-rounds.

title: AI Shields Kids By Revolutionizing Child Safety And Online Protection
text:
In the digital age, where technology permeates every aspect of our lives, the protection of the most vulnerable among us, our children, has taken on new dimensions and challenges. Artificial intelligence (AI) emerges as an ally of hope, a tool not just for advancement but as a guardian in the complex web of the online world. Let’s explore the myriad ways AI is harnessed to create a safer environment for children, highlighting real-world applications and the promise they hold for the future.
AI: The Guardian of the Digital Playground
The Internet, with all its resources and opportunities for learning and connection, also harbors risks for young users. AI technology steps in as a vigilant protector, monitoring and analyzing online content at a scale and speed impossible for human moderators alone. By filtering harmful content, detecting predatory behavior, and providing educational resources, AI acts as a guardian of the digital playground, ensuring it remains a space of safety and growth for children.
Detecting and Filtering Harmful Content
One of the most straightforward yet impactful applications of AI in child protection is the detection and filtering of harmful online content. Companies like Google and Facebook employ sophisticated AI algorithms that scan millions of posts, images, and videos daily, flagging and removing content that could be harmful to children. These systems are trained on vast datasets to recognize inappropriate material, ensuring that the digital spaces children navigate are free from exploitation and abuse.
Combating Cyberbullying with AI
Cyberbullying is a pervasive issue in the online world, affecting countless children and adolescents. AI technology offers a proactive solution, identifying bullying behavior in texts, emails, and social media interactions. Platforms like Instagram have implemented AI tools that detect potentially offensive comments before they are posted, prompting the user to reconsider. This application of AI not only stops cyberbullying in its tracks but also promotes a culture of kindness and reflection among young internet users.
AI and the Fight Against Child Exploitation
In the critical fight against child exploitation, AI has become an invaluable ally. Organizations such as Thorn and the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC) leverage AI to identify and rescue victims of child trafficking and sexual exploitation. Thorn's AI-driven tool, Safer, helps tech companies identify and remove child sexual abuse material (CSAM) from their platforms. By analyzing images and videos at scale, these AI systems assist in the swift identification of victims, leading to their rescue and the apprehension of perpetrators.
Educational AI: Fostering Safe Online Habits
AI's role in protecting children extends into education, where it serves as a guide in fostering safe online habits. Platforms like Interland, an AI powered game developed by Google, teach children about internet safety in an engaging and interactive way. Through gameplay, children learn to recognize phishing, secure their personal information, and navigate the Internet responsibly, equipping them with the knowledge to protect themselves online.
AI-Assisted Parental Monitoring
Parental monitoring apps have integrated AI to help guardians keep their children safe online without invading their privacy. These apps alert parents to potential risks, such as cyberbullying or contact with strangers, while respecting the child's autonomy and privacy. By analyzing communication patterns and content, AI gives parents peace of mind, knowing they have the tools to protect their children in the digital age.
The Ethical Use of AI in Child Protection
As we leverage AI to protect children, the ethical considerations of privacy, consent, and data security are paramount. The development and deployment of AI in this field must be guided by strict ethical standards, ensuring that technology serves the best interests of children without compromising their rights or autonomy. In addition, keeping kids safe requires an ecosystem of family, children, teachers, regulators, and lawmakers to enact the safeguards so that we can maximize the protection of children.
The Future of Child Protection with AI
Looking ahead, the AI integration in child protection holds limitless potential. As AI technology evolves, its capacity to understand context, recognize nuances in behavior, and predict risks will only improve, offering even more robust protection for children. The collaboration between technology companies, non-profits, governments, and communities is essential in driving this progress forward, ensuring that as the digital landscape evolves, our children remain safe and supported.
Thus, AI stands as a testament to technology's power to do good, to protect and uplift the most vulnerable members of our society. Through its ability to monitor, educate, and intervene, AI is reshaping the landscape of child protection, offering hope and security in a world fraught with digital risks. As we continue to harness AI for the benefit of children, we are reminded of our collective responsibility to safeguard their innocence and ensure their digital experiences are enriching, not endangering. The future of child protection lies in the balance of technology and humanity, a future where every child can explore, learn, and grow with the digital world as their playground, guarded by the vigilant, caring eyes of AI.

title: Artificial intelligence detects cancer with 17% more accuracy than doctors in UCLA study
text:
Artificial intelligence detects cancer with 17% more accuracy than doctors in UCLA study
The Unfold AI software helps ensure ‘more accurate diagnoses and targeted treatments,’ experts say
Artificial intelligence is outpacing doctors when it comes to detecting a common cancer in men.
A new study from UCLA found that an AI tool identified prostate cancer with 84% accuracy — compared to 67% accuracy for cases detected by physicians, according to a press release from the university.
Unfold AI, made by Avenda Health in California — a software recently cleared by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration — uses an AI algorithm to visualize the likelihood of cancer based on various types of clinical data.
WHAT IS ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE?
In the study, a team of seven urologists and three radiologists analyzed 50 cases where tumors had been removed, looking for signs of residual cancer.
A few months later, the AI software performed the same analysis.
The "negative margin rate" — a medical term that describes the absence of cancer cells surrounding the removed tissue — was 45 times greater in AI-detected cases, so the chances of cancer being left behind was far less.
Ali Kasraeian, M.D., a urologist at Kasraeian Urology in Jacksonville, Florida, said he uses the Unfold AI technology in his consultations with patients about managing their prostate cancer.
AI COULD PREDICT WHETHER CANCER TREATMENTS WILL WORK, EXPERTS SAY: ‘EXCITING TIME IN MEDICINE'
"The AI takes the information that we currently have about a patient's prostate cancer — like their pathology, imaging and biopsy results — and creates a 3D cancer estimation map," he told Fox News Digital via email.
"The results we get from Unfold AI tell us if a patient will be better suited for focal therapy or more radical therapy, such as radical prostatectomy, or radiation therapy, ensuring we optimize their cancer cure, the personalization of their cancer care, and their quality of life goals."
"AI is our new diagnostic ally — but like any tool, it works best in human hands."
Based on these findings, the AI could lead to more accurate diagnoses and more targeted treatments, reducing the need for full-gland removal and the side effects that can come with it, such as incontinence and impotence, the researchers wrote.
AI MODEL COULD HELP PREDICT LUNG CANCER RISKS IN NON-SMOKERS, STUDY FINDS: ‘SIGNIFICANT ADVANCEMENT’
Joshua Trachenberg, PhD, is a professor of neurobiology at UCLA — and also a prostate cancer patient himself. After doctors found a slow-growing tumor on his prostate, they recommended removing the gland surgically — but he decided to explore other options.
"I got in touch with a team at UCLA, where I also am a faculty member, that was exploring alternate treatments to total gland removal," Trachenberg, 56, told Fox News Digital via email.
The UCLA researchers were testing an approach that uses ultrasound to heat tissue and is "focally guided" by MRI to destroy the cancerous tissue without damaging the rest of the gland, he said.
After some imaging scans, it was determined that Trachenberg was a candidate for the experimental therapy.
AI TECH AIMS TO DETECT BREAST CANCER BY MIMICKING RADIOLOGISTS’ EYE MOVEMENTS: 'A CRITICAL FRIEND'
"The 3D map created by Unfold AI enabled this team to identify precise margins, target the cancerous area and avoid any functional structures of the gland," he said.
"It was able to visualize my cancer and it gave me a much better understanding of my case."
"It was truly able to visualize my cancer and it gave me a much better understanding of my case."
Trachenberg is now cancer-free and was able to avoid a radical prostatectomy.
"So many men are afraid of treatment because of the risks associated with gland removal, and Unfold AI enables therapies that don’t put men through the meat grinder," he said.
This type of AI technology gives Trachenberg hope for the future of prostate cancer treatment, he told Fox News Digital.

"Too often, we are given only two options: Watch and wait for it to get worse, or take the entire gland out, which often leaves men with lifelong side effects that strain their physical health, emotional health and even their marriages," he said.
"I would recommend to any prostate cancer patient who is told they need a radical prostatectomy that they take some time to look at all their options, [including] AI technologies."
Potential risks, limitations
Dr. Harvey Castro, a board-certified emergency medicine physician and national speaker on artificial intelligence based in Dallas, Texas, was not involved in the new study but shared his insights on the potential risks associated with the technology.
"The accuracy of AI depends heavily on the quality of the data it is trained on," he told Fox News Digital. "Poor data can lead to inaccurate diagnoses."

Castro also cautioned against an "overreliance" on AI.
"While AI is a powerful tool, it should complement, not replace, the clinical judgment of health care professionals," he said.
"AI is our new diagnostic ally," Castro added. "But like any tool, it works best in human hands."
Privacy should also be considered when using this type of technology, according to Castro.
"Handling sensitive patient data with AI necessitates stringent data protection measures to maintain patient trust and confidentiality."

The cost of AI technologies can also be a significant barrier, added Kasraeian.
"I hope this study encourages us and future payers to make these innovations more accessible to urologists and, most importantly, to our patients."
