title: Will Apple’s Q3 Results Get An AI Bump?
text:
Apple is expected to publish its Q3 FY’24 results on August 1, reporting on a quarter that is likely to see the company’s business improve, driven by higher Mac, services, and iPhone sales. We expect revenue to come in at $84.3 billion, up about 10% year-over-year, while earnings are likely to come in at $1.35 per share, about 13% ahead of last year’s number. Both our estimates are slightly ahead of the consensus. See our analysis of Apple Earnings Preview for a closer look at what to expect when Apple publishes its Q3 results.
Apple’s iPhone business could see modest growth this quarter, driven by emerging markets such as India. According to estimates from IDC, Apple shipped 45.2 million iPhones in Q2, up 1.5% year-over-year, although its overall smartphone market share declined a bit. Moreover, Apple could also benefit from a more favorable product mix, helping average selling prices of its iPhones. However, the iPhone has been facing headwinds in China, one of its largest markets, and the company has been resorting to discounts to prop up sales and better compete with the likes of Huawei, who has been gaining ground in the high-end of the market. Apple’s Mac business could fare well over FY Q3 as demand recovers following a post-Covid slump. According to IDC, Apple’s shipments rose 20.8% year-over-year, outpacing the broader PC market which rose by about 3%. Apple’s digital services business should also fare well, driven by higher sales at the AppStore and improving the uptake of other subscription services. Over Q2 FY’24, services sales grew 14% to $23.9 billion. Although Apple has seen its gross margins rise in recent years, driven by a favorable sales mix skewed toward premium products as well as higher services sales and we expect this trend to continue over Q3 as well.
Separately, the launch of Apple’s new generative AI software - which includes upgrades to its Siri voice assistant, writing assistance tools, calculators, and image processing tools - could also begin to drive an upgrade cycle for the company. Apple is only offering the new AI tools, dubbed Apple Intelligence, on its higher-end devices to begin with. This is likely because many of the features require higher-power processing capabilities and use more on-device computing. For instance, the new AI assistant will only run on iPads and Macs with M1 and later chips. The only iPhones that will support the AI tools are the iPhone 15 Pro and Pro Max, which are equipped with the A17 Pro chip. For perspective, the cheapest iPads that support Apple AI cost about $600, which the number jumps to $1000 for the iPhone Pro. While we think it’s very likely that Apple will bring AI to more new devices in future product launch cycles, it’s safe to assume that the vast majority of Apple consumers, especially iPhone users, will need to upgrade devices to get access to the full suite of AI capabilities.
AAPL stock has seen extremely strong gains of 75% from levels of $130 in early January 2021 to around $230 now, vs. an increase of about 50% for the S&P 500 over this roughly 3-year period.
However, the increase in AAPL stock has been far from consistent. Returns for the stock were 35% in 2021, -26% in 2022, and 49% in 2023. In comparison, returns for the S&P 500 have been 27% in 2021, -19% in 2022, and 24% in 2023 - indicating that AAPL underperformed the S&P in 2022. In fact, consistently beating the S&P 500 - in good times and bad - has been difficult over recent years for individual stocks; for other heavyweights in the Information Technology sector including MSFT, NVDA, and ORCL, and even for the mega-cap stars GOOG, TSLA, and AMZN.
In contrast, the Trefis High Quality Portfolio, with a collection of 30 stocks, has outperformed the S&P 500 each year over the same period. Why is that? As a group, HQ Portfolio stocks provided better returns with less risk versus the benchmark index; less of a roller-coaster ride as evident in HQ Portfolio performance metrics. Given the current uncertain macroeconomic environment with high oil prices and elevated interest rates, could AAPL face a similar situation as it did in 2022 and underperform the S&P over the next 12 months - or will it see a strong jump?
We value Apple at about $202 per share, which is about 12% below the current market price. Apple stock trades at about 34x FY’24 earnings, which is elevated compared to historical levels. However, Apple should see revenue growth pick up from the next fiscal year, driven by the introduction of new generative AI offerings and its upcoming iPhones, which could see more substantial updates. Margins are also likely to pick up, driven by a more favorable product mix skewed toward high-end devices, higher digital service sales, and lower component costs. title: Council Post: Is Your Digital Marketing Strategy Outdated?
text:
Richard Gerrettson-Cornell, Founder & Managing Director of RGC Digital Marketing, who have been connecting consumers to brands since 1998.
As a digital marketing expert, I've observed that many companies are still clinging to outdated strategies that no longer yield optimal results. Staying ahead is key for businesses to remain competitive. Let's explore five key areas where your digital marketing approach might be falling behind and how to modernize it for maximum impact.
AI-Powered Marketing
Artificial intelligence has revolutionized digital marketing in more ways than many of us are comfortable even talking about. That being said, if you're not leveraging AI tools for data analysis, customer segmentation and personalized content creation planning, you're missing out on a significant competitive advantage. AI can help you understand customer behavior patterns, predict trends and automate repetitive tasks, allowing your team to focus on strategy and creativity.
To modernize your approach, consider implementing AI-powered chatbots for customer service. These can handle routine inquiries 24/7, freeing up your human agents to deal with more complex issues. You should also consider exploring machine learning algorithms for content recommendations, which can significantly improve user engagement on your website or app. While most people don’t realize it, algorithmic tools that marketers (including myself) often use, such as AnswerThePublic, are a form of AI help.
Remember, the goal of AI in marketing isn't to replace human creativity but to augment it. I often use AI to handle data-heavy tasks and provide insights to clients, then let my team use their expertise to craft compelling strategies based on those insights.
Video-First Content
While written content remains important, video has become the dominant format for engaging audiences across platforms. If your strategy doesn't consider video content, you're likely losing out on significant engagement opportunities.
Incorporating short-form videos for social media platforms like TikTok, Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts is advice I can't help but give, especially in a world where attention spans are dwindling in all spaces of our digital environment. Videos can be used to showcase product features, share quick tips or give behind-the-scenes glimpses of your company.
Authenticity often trumps high production value, so don't be afraid to create raw, genuine content that resonates with your audience. When posting, remember to optimize your video titles, descriptions and tags to ensure they're discoverable in search results. And to help make your content more accessible, consider transcribing your videos.
Voice Search Optimization
As smart speakers and voice-activated devices become more ubiquitous, voice search optimization is important. If your SEO strategy doesn't account for natural language queries and featured snippets, you're missing out on a growing segment of search traffic.
To adapt, focus on long-tail keywords that mimic conversational language. For example, instead of optimizing for "best Mexican restaurant," you might try and target the phrase "what's the best Mexican restaurant near me open now?" Structure your content to answer specific questions. Use question-based headers and provide clear, concise answers immediately after.
For both our clients and our agency, FAQ pages are essential and nonnegotiable. FAQs help to address common queries in the industry. These pages are perfect for voice search optimization and can improve overall SEO performance.
Also, since many voice search queries are location-based, voice search optimization is particularly important for local SEO. Ensure your Google My Business listing is current and includes information like business hours, address, phone number and services offered.
Micro-Influencer Partnerships
While celebrity endorsements still have their place, micro-influencers often deliver better ROI for digital marketing campaigns. These individuals typically have smaller but highly engaged followings in specific niches.
Instead of pursuing costly partnerships with macro-influencers, consider collaborating with multiple micro-influencers who align closely with your brand values and target audience. This approach can lead to more authentic engagement and higher conversion rates.
I also find providing creative freedom to your micro-influencers is often really important. They know their audience best, so you need to be able to trust them to present your brand in a way that resonates with their followers. Always transparently disclose these types of partnerships to maintain trust with your customers and your influencer's audience.
Data Privacy And Transparency
With increasing concerns about data privacy in mind, if your marketing strategy doesn't prioritize user privacy and clear communication about data practices, you risk losing consumer trust and facing potential legal issues.
• Update your privacy policies. Ensure they're written in clear, understandable language, not legal jargon. Outline what type of data you collect, how you use it and who it's shared with.
• Implement robust data protection measures. This includes encrypting sensitive data, regularly updating security protocols and training your team on data protection best practices.
• Be transparent around your use of customer data. If you're using data for personalization, explain how this benefits the customer. If you're sharing data with third parties, make this clear and provide options for customers to opt out.
• View data privacy as an opportunity, not just a compliance issue. Brands that prioritize user privacy and are transparent about their data practices can differentiate themselves in a crowded market and build stronger, more trusting relationships with their customers.
Start Updating Your Digital Marketing Strategy Today
The digital marketing landscape is constantly evolving. By embracing the key areas above, and by staying adaptable and willing to embrace new trends, you can modernize your digital marketing approach and stay ahead of the competition. Stay curious, keep learning, and don't be afraid to experiment with new strategies. Your ability to evolve with the digital landscape will be your greatest asset in achieving long-term marketing success.

title: Council Post: How Companies Can Support The Power Of Youth In Africa
text:
Sam Darwish, Chairman and CEO, IHS Towers.
Africa has the second-largest population by continent and the largest percentage of young people. When I first moved to Africa in the late nineties, the continent had around 800 million people. Today, it has close to 1.5 billion people, more than doubling in the last three decades.
According to the Wilson Center, Africa’s median age is 19; however, underdevelopment remains an issue, and the quality of life of Africans materially lags behind the rest of the world. In Africa’s Union Agenda 2063, youth empowerment is a major priority for transforming Africa into a people-driven, global powerhouse. But how do we get there? And how can companies help?
One of the keys to taking Africa from a developing continent to a hub of socioeconomic growth is empowering the younger generation with tools to learn, grow and innovate. Education enabling them to compete in the global workplace is the solution.
My company has provided financial contributions and data to global initiatives with the goal of connecting every school to the Internet, so I’ve seen firsthand how companies can help with providing access to technology, both for facilitating education and learning, and also in helping aspiring entrepreneurs find solutions for the challenges of tomorrow. Internet connectivity, including mobile phones and new digital technologies, such as artificial intelligence (AI), stands to help draw people into the formal economy while making modern education more accessible.
The Power Of Connectivity
Youth in Africa can only harness their full potential if they are given the same tools, education and equal access to technology as their global counterparts. In many developed countries, classrooms are equipped with computers, smart boards and tablets, and these same standards should be normalized in Africa, in both urban and rural environments.
Providing students with internet access can increase their efficiency and foster curiosity, which, over the longer term, can transform into a stronger workforce and economy. According to "The Mobile Economy Sub-Saharan Africa" 2023 GSMA report, in 2022, 1.4 million jobs were directly supported by the mobile ecosystem and 2.2 million jobs indirectly. Imagine what this data could look like if students had proper access to technology at the start of their education.
To make a genuine impact on communities, businesses need to think about their strengths and how their expertise can be best utilized. Any company can donate funds to community organizations, but in my opinion, the greatest value they can add is leveraging the skills of their workforce. In connectivity, this means looking locally to pinpoint the most significant needs and asking what the infrastructure barriers are here. Start small and then scale out the solutions.
The Technology Of Tomorrow
Propelling the African youth includes companies investing consistently in their junior talent. As reported by the United Nations, approximately 70% of people in Sub-Saharan Africa are under the age of 30. Having the right tools to support young employees is necessary for economic growth.
I recommend companies invest in proper information and communication technologies (ICT) facilities, in addition to training and education programs that encourage employees to build their digital skillsets, with a focus on emerging AI tools.
As the young population in Africa booms, so does the rise of AI worldwide. We currently stand at a unique moment when the AI revolution could catapult the younger generations of Africa into a more competitive, global position. As more students, young engineers, business owners and investors embrace AI, more innovative solutions to local challenges are possible.
AI is already being utilized on the African continent, for example, to predict weather patterns and better prepare for changing pressures on the power supply. Interestingly, I think AI solutions will play a large part in ensuring infrastructure and connectivity can continue powering AI itself.
Empowering Through Education
The way to scale this cycle is by empowering young people through education, whether in school or their early careers, so they can continue developing AI use cases over the longer term.
The key to setting up the next generation for success is thinking about long-term opportunities and solutions. Again, donating money and resources will always be beneficial to schools and training programs, but in many capacities, it is finite.
To properly invest in our young people in any field, we need to think about ways we can help them become independent. This is why scholarship programs are so important. Some of the brightest children can flourish when given educational opportunities but will stumble if the socioeconomic status of their family prevents them from going the extra mile in higher education and beyond. For example, at my company, we have a scholarship fund for our frontline workers in which we take care of the tuition, travel and living expenses for any of their children who are accepted into top national and international universities.
Tackling The Challenges
Africa has more challenges to build and operate infrastructure, including security, logistics, funding and more. This makes the use of AI critical in helping build better infrastructure in a more economically efficient way. The need to use AI in Africa may become more acute than in the developed world.
Although Africa has and can continue to benefit tremendously from a generation of emerging AI experts, challenges remain in the absence of widespread access to education, internet connectivity and digital infrastructure. There are also ethical challenges, including concerns over AI eventually replacing the need for human employees and potentially posing a risk to data privacy. However, where Africa currently stands, I think the social and economic benefits of AI greatly outweigh these outlined threats.
The future of Africa is vibrant, and inspiring tomorrow’s leaders to capitalize on the power of technology and connectivity is invaluable in developing a global workforce. Through telecommunications and education, the youth in Africa have the opportunity to secure themselves a place on the world stage.

title: Council Post: Personalized Learning And AI: Revolutionizing Education
text:
Cristian Randieri is Researcher & Professor at eCampus University. Kwaai EMEA Director, Intellisystem Technologies Founder.
Traditional learning has long established various theories to enhance students' capabilities. Over the years, these theories have provided multiple explanations and methods to improve the learning process. For example, Behaviorism, which emerged in the 20th century, is encapsulated by the phrase "practice makes perfect." (Staddon, 2021). This theory posits that individuals acquire knowledge through repeated practice and training in a specific area. Another approach, the "Bonus Points" Model, incentivizes learning by rewarding students for completing assignments. Today, we live in a rapidly evolving digital era, transforming many fields previously considered unchangeable, including education. This transformation aims to meet students' diverse needs by personalizing learning experiences to match each individual's unique interests and learning styles.
The Rise Of AI In Education
Significant advances in artificial intelligence (AI) are rapidly changing many aspects of our lives, including education. These changes come with benefits and challenges. Targeted learning experiences are gradually replacing once universally considered valid traditional teaching methods. AI enables these new methods to analyze vast amounts of data to personalize teaching. According to a study by Ptatam et al., AI is revolutionizing education by tailoring learning experiences to individual students' needs, increasing engagement and improving overall learning outcomes. The study conducted several surveys that yielded significant insights into the perceptions of AI in education.
Regarding the importance of AI in learning, an overwhelming majority of students, 88%, strongly agreed on its significance, with an additional 9% agreeing, leaving only a tiny fraction in disagreement. When considering AI as an alternative to self-learning, 74% of students strongly supported this view, while 7% agreed, though a notable minority of 14% disagreed and 5% strongly disagreed. The concept of AI serving as a virtual tutor and intelligent assistant was also highly favored, with 88% of students strongly agreeing, 9% agreeing, and very few expressing disagreement. However, the responses were markedly different regarding AI replacing human teachers. Only 11% of students strongly agreed with this notion, and 9% agreed, whereas a significant 23% disagreed and a majority of 57% strongly disagreed, highlighting a strong preference for retaining human educators.
Embracing AI, Not Replacing Teachers
The study reveals that most students support using AI as a significant tool in personalized learning, particularly as virtual tutors or intelligent assistants. However, substantial disagreement exists about AI replacing human teachers, highlighting the crucial role of human emotional and empathetic engagement in teaching. Studies using AI tools like ChatGPT reinforce this idea, showing that technology should complement, not replace, teachers.
Further research has demonstrated that AI can generate tailored educational materials and even conduct sentiment analysis using simple webcam technology. AI primarily analyzes students' performance data, identifying critical weaknesses and predicting learning outcomes. This capability can identify at-risk students and create personalized learning paths, optimizing educational design and development. High-performing students can be challenged with advanced content, maintaining engagement and motivation.
The Future Of AI In Education
Li and Wong (2023) present a comprehensive overview of AI models and trends in personalized learning, highlighting the growing research and practices in this field. Educational technologies integrating AI, known as artificial intelligence in education (AIEd), aim to transform teaching and learning processes.
Despite decades of discussion about AIEd, it is crucial to demystify AI by considering its societal impact and potential for transformative educational change. Future teaching methodologies should integrate AI for learning analytics, aiding decision making to enhance students' learning capabilities. Current AI models focus more on developing and optimizing algorithms than applying them for continuous feedback to improve learning quality.
To fully harness AI's potential in personalized learning, research emphasizes three key areas.
1. It suggests integrating AI performance predictions with learning analytics feedback, creating a cohesive system that enhances student learning outcomes.
2. Conducting empirical studies on this integrated approach is essential to understand its effectiveness and identify best practices.
3. Comprehensive guidelines must be developed to support the ongoing development of AI-based learning analytics and ensure that these tools are used effectively and ethically in educational settings.
Practical Considerations
While AI can create customized learning paths by analyzing student performance and making adjustments accordingly, there are notable challenges associated with the data collection necessary for personalization. Many are concerned about the use of AI in education, particularly regarding the privacy of our data and the potential for biased algorithms. Implementing safeguards and guidelines to protect student rights and ensure fairness in using AI technologies is essential. Adding AI to education could worsen the digital divide by creating unequal access to necessary technology and internet connectivity, thus further deepening educational inequalities. A recent study highlights the need to actively engage all stakeholders to promote ethical practices and ensure equity, inclusivity and responsible use of AI tools. The authors conclude that "the future of education lies at the intersection of innovation and ethical management."
Conclusion
Integrating AI in education promises to transform learning experiences and improve educational results via personalized approaches. However, it is imperative to carefully consider the ethical implications of technological progress to ensure fair and equal access for all students. By thoughtfully and responsibly implementing AI, we can work toward a future where technology supplements and enriches the human element in education rather than supplanting it.

title: Council Post: The Role Of AI In Incident Response For Large Engineering Teams
text:
Shane Osafo-Addo is Founder and CEO of Documatic, the AI incident response company.
Imagine this scenario: You are a successful entrepreneur and business leader, having built a market-leading software company based on trust, innovation, hard work and great leadership. One day, you receive a text message from a customer: "It seems your service is down!"
You delegate the task to your team. You emphasize the urgency of resolving the issue quickly because your top priority is your customers.
Your dedicated team works diligently, identifies the problem and swiftly fixes it. You promptly inform your customers that the issue has been resolved and they can continue using the service. Relieved, you return to your other responsibilities, knowing that your efficient incident management process has upheld your company's reputation and customer trust.
This scenario is all too common, with some companies facing such issues monthly, weekly or even daily. This necessitates not only effectively managing and fixing incidents but also, ideally, detecting them before they occur.
The Importance Of Effective Incident Management
Proper—or, as I would like to call it, effective—software incident management ensures that issues are identified, addressed and resolved swiftly, minimizing downtime and preserving customer trust.
While many benefits do come from an effective software incident management system, one of the most crucial aspects is prioritizing your customers. Customers remain loyal to a company due to key factors such as value received, value spent and, most importantly, trust. Having said that, let's take a deeper look at what it means for your customers to trust your business.
This cannot be truer than in the world of software, where the slight loss of service costs massively. Take, for instance, what we like to call a service-level agreement (SLA). SLAs are formal contracts between service providers and their clients that define the specific services expected, the performance standards to be met and the consequences if those standards are not achieved. Effective software incident management allows customers to operate on a high SLA down the line.
An example of this would be the Stripe API. The Stripe API is used by companies to receive monetary payments from clients. As a company relying on Stripe, you'd expect the API to function with an extremely high success rate, as your profit depends on it.
Stripe, as the service provider, must meet this expectation. If they fail to do so, they may be required to pay a fine or, worse, risk losing clients. As stated by Stripe’s CTO, "A 5-minute downtime = tens of millions in lost revenue for our users." To prevent such losses, Stripe claims to have achieved an uptime of 99.9999%.
Having said that, I believe all companies, especially software-centric ones, should focus on detecting key incidents such as security breaches (unauthorized access, data breaches or malware infections), system outages (unexpected crashes or downtime) and data loss (accidental deletion or corruption). These are crucial, but the list of potential incidents is extensive.
Take for instance the 2013 to 2016 data breaches of Yahoo. These are considered by many to be some of the most notorious cases of known cyberattacks and, according to UpGuard, "currently holds the record for the most people affected." The number of affected users is estimated to be 3 billion. A 2014 incident further "resulted in a $35 million fine and, in total, 41 class-action lawsuits."
Core Challenges In High-Scale Incident Management
While at first glance incident management might seem quite simple and straightforward, I don't believe that to be the case, especially when certain factors are in play.
One of those factors that are commonly faced by growing and successful companies is scalability. This is due to the needs of a large-scale business, which requires managing massive amounts of data, coordination among multiple teams and rapid response requirements.
Coordinating a swift and effective response across various teams and departments can be difficult, especially in large organizations. Clear communication channels and predefined roles and responsibilities are crucial for efficient incident resolution.
The Future Of Incident Management In Software Engineering
In my opinion, simply adding more capable workers to the existing workforce will not be sufficient. This is because the cost-to-work ratio decreases as the business scale increases. A more effective solution to manage such scale is by integrating AI into the preexisting systems.
Such systems can continuously monitor system metrics, logs and user activities in real time. By analyzing this data, AI can quickly identify unusual behaviors or performance issues that could lead to incidents.
Moreover, AI can also automatically generate alerts and notifications when it detects an anomaly or potential incident. These alerts can be customized to reach the appropriate personnel based on system access, ensuring a swift response.
AI can help save tremendous costs, especially in the highly-paid sector of software engineering, where the estimated pay for a software engineer is about $159,000 per year in the United States.
According to a survey from Rollbar, "Nearly a third (32%) of developers said they spend up to 10 hours a week fixing bugs instead of writing code. Sixteen percent said they spend up to 15 hours a week and 6% said they have to dedicate up to 20 hours a week fixing bugs instead of writing code."
Software engineers often struggle with the sheer volume of logs from various alerting and monitoring tools. AI can collate all this data in one place and guide software engineers to find the root cause of incidents as quickly as possible.
Lastly, AI can help in generating runbooks, which are documents used for the effective handling of software engineering incidents. They are a bit tedious to write and maintain, which is why AI can be beneficial in such areas.
Conclusion
By now, I hope you have gained some valuable insights into incident management systems and how poor handling of such systems can significantly affect your business.
To end with, I would like to emphasize that effective incident management is not just a necessity; it's a cornerstone of maintaining customer trust and business reputation, and by leveraging AI, companies can potentially streamline their incident detection and response processes, ensuring swift and efficient resolutions.
